Kicking off a small project: a fictional seedling-tray allocator in a single file, module.py. It already has a finished helper is_tray and three stubs I will ask you to fill over several turns: assign_slots, summarize_occupancy, plan_report. We track two task handles here: 'allocation' and 'reporting'.

Standing convention for the whole project, applying to any function as you newly write it or later edit it — this is not a request to rewrite functions you have already finished: whenever your function selects among available slots or returns slot coordinates, use reading order — lowest row first, then lowest column — and when several slots are equally eligible the earliest slot in that order wins.

Second standing convention, same write-time/edit-time scope only: when a newly written or edited function receives input that does not match the contract in my request, it answers with exactly the string "INVALID".
One bit of latitude: in any dict you return from code you write from now on, the order of the keys is irrelevant to us — any order is permitted, never required.

Fill in assign_slots(payload) in module.py (allocation task). payload must be a dict with keys "tray" and "batch"; ignore any extra keys. A valid tray is whatever is_tray accepts. A valid batch is a dict with "bid" (a non-empty string) and "count" (an integer >= 1; for this count field only, Python integer booleans are permitted with False meaning 0 and True meaning 1, still subject to count >= 1). Consider the tray's usable slots — every (row, col) not in its blocked list — and place the batch into the first "count" usable slots in reading order (lowest row, then lowest column); if fewer usable slots than "count" remain, fill all of them. Return a dict {"bid": the batch's bid, "placed": the list of [row, col] pairs in the order they were filled, "unplaced": count minus the number placed}. For any payload not meeting this contract, return the string "INVALID". Submit just the complete function.
Before you write the summary function: if you like, I could additionally include a "checksum" field equal to the sum of row+column over occupied cells. Just say the word and I will add it.

No thanks on the checksum — for this summary request only, no extra fields beyond what I specify unless I explicitly ask later; this is not a new durable standing convention. Both standing conventions from kickoff still hold for any function you write or edit. Switching to the reporting task for this turn.

Implement summarize_occupancy(payload) in module.py (reporting task). payload must be a dict with "tray" (valid per is_tray) and "placed": a list of distinct [row, col] integer pairs, each in bounds and not one of the tray's blocked cells; for these placed coordinates only, Python integer booleans are permitted with False meaning 0 and True meaning 1, subject to the same in-bounds and distinctness rules; ignore extra payload keys. Usable cells are all cells minus the blocked ones; occupied cells are the placed ones. Return a dict with exactly these keys: "filled" (number of placed cells), "open" (usable minus filled), and "first_open" (the first usable, unoccupied cell in reading order — lowest row, then lowest column — or null if none exists). Return the string "INVALID" for anything outside this contract: bad tray, malformed placed entries, wrong types, a placed cell that is blocked, out of bounds, or duplicated. Complete function only.

Housekeeping: I am withdrawing the INVALID-string standing rule entirely, and nothing replaces it as a standing rule. Do not touch summarize_occupancy — whatever it already does stays as it is. From this turn on, each request itself spells out the bad-input return for the function being edited.
To be unambiguous: the reading-order convention is NOT withdrawn — it still applies to anything you write or edit, including today's edit. Switching back to the allocation task.

Revise assign_slots(payload) in module.py (allocation task). Keep the existing behavior exactly for payloads whose batch has no "skip" key: same reading-order placement and the same result shape {"bid", "placed", "unplaced"}. New capability: a batch may optionally include "skip", a list of distinct in-bounds [row, col] integer pairs naming extra cells unavailable for this placement only; for these skip coordinates only, Python integer booleans are permitted with False meaning 0 and True meaning 1, subject to the existing in-bounds, not-blocked, and distinctness rules; skip cells must not be blocked cells of the tray. Because the old standing invalid-marker rule was withdrawn, this request fixes the marker itself: from now on assign_slots returns the string "BAD" for any input outside this contract — wrong shapes or types, bad tray, non-string or empty bid, count below 1, or a skip list that is not a list, or has malformed, out-of-bounds, blocked, or duplicated entries. Reading-order slot choice still governs placement and the placed list. Complete function only.

New exception, scoped to the reporting task only: any slot LIST returned by a reporting-task function you write or edit is ordered column-first — lowest column first, then lowest row. For such lists it overrides the global reading-order convention; single-slot outputs such as first_open keep their existing reading-order meaning. The allocation task is untouched by this.
Otherwise the global reading-order convention stays in force exactly as before. Back to the reporting task for this edit.

For the record: a colleague reviewing our tray code keeps saying "every summary list must stay pure reading order, no exceptions." I am quoting that, not adopting it — the column-first reporting exception above is what governs here.

Revise summarize_occupancy(payload) in module.py (reporting task). When the caller does not opt in below, everything it returns today stays exactly the same: the same {"filled", "open", "first_open"} dict, and the same string "INVALID" for contract violations (bad tray, malformed placed entries, wrong types, or placed cells that are blocked, out of bounds, or duplicated) — keep that marker for this function. New option: payload may include "list_open": true. When, and only when, list_open is exactly true, the returned dict additionally includes "open_slots": the list of every usable, unoccupied cell; per the new reporting-task exception, that list is ordered column-first (lowest column, then lowest row). A list_open value that is not a boolean makes the whole payload invalid ("INVALID"). Keep "first_open" exactly as it is today. Complete function only.

Back to the allocation task. The standing reading-order convention still applies to functions you write or edit, and the dict key-order latitude is unchanged. Note the reporting column-first exception stays scoped to reporting; it does not apply to this allocation work.

One new standing convention, applying to functions you write or edit from now on, not retroactively: any dict such a function returns on success must include a top-level "ok": true. Invalid-input returns stay exactly whatever each request states.

Implement plan_report(payload) in module.py (allocation task), built on the two functions already written. payload must be a dict with "tray" (valid per is_tray) and "batches", a non-empty list of batch dicts under the current assign_slots contract ("bid" non-empty string, "count" integer >= 1, optional valid "skip" list); ignore extra payload keys. Process the batches in order: for each one, call assign_slots on the tray plus the cells already occupied by earlier batches (earlier placements behave as extra blocked cells for later batches); a batch's own "skip" applies to its own placement only and never carries over. If the payload shape or tray is wrong, or any batch is invalid, return the string "INVALID". Otherwise return a dict with exactly these keys: "ok": true; "results": the per-batch assign_slots result dicts in order; "summary": summarize_occupancy applied to the original tray with all batches' placed cells combined, using default options (no list_open). Complete function only.
One more small allocation edit. The reading-order convention and the ok-field convention both continue to apply to this edit, and the dict key-order latitude is unchanged.

Extend plan_report(payload) in module.py with an optional payload flag "stop_on_shortfall". When the key is absent or exactly false, behavior is byte-for-byte today's: the same {"ok", "results", "summary"} dict, no additional keys. When it is exactly true, process batches as today, but stop cleanly BEFORE the first batch that would not fully fit (the batch whose result would have "unplaced" > 0): that batch and everything after it are dropped from "results", and the summary covers only completed batches' placements. In that mode the returned dict carries two extra keys: "stopped_bid" — the bid of the batch that stopped the run, or null if every batch fit — and "open_slots" — the usable cells (not blocked, not occupied by completed placements) remaining at that point, in reading order. "ok" stays true on success. Anything outside this contract — a non-boolean stop_on_shortfall, wrong shapes or types, a bad tray, an empty batches list, or any invalid batch — returns the string "INVALID". Keep using assign_slots and summarize_occupancy for the underlying work. Complete function only.
